Its hallmark in those years was the 'actio popularis': anyone could challenge a law without proving personal standing (the rules have changed since).

old: Sólyom coined the doctrine of the *láthatatlan alkotmány* (invisible constitution): the idea that constitutional adjudication must follow a coherent, morally grounded system of fundamental principles that transcends the literal text of the written constitution.
new: Sólyom used the idea of the *láthatatlan alkotmány* (invisible constitution) in his 1990 concurring opinion on the death penalty: the idea that the court draws on a coherent system of fundamental principles that goes beyond the literal text of the constitution.
why: claim "coined" and strong wording softened; paraphrase, not a quotation (check)
